A-01.name: Splash / breathing load
A-01.intent: Set the emotional register before any UI: three concentric circles breathe around the wordmark at 7s, roughly a calm respiratory cycle. Covers session restore, feature-flag fetch and locale detection.
A-01.layers:
Splash
├ Background / sandstone
├ BreathingRings
│ ├ Ring 300 (0s)
│ ├ Ring 220 (0.6s)
│ └ Ring 150 (1.2s)
├ Logo / hoy lockup
├ Tagline
└ LoadState
  ├ Spinner
  └ Label

A-02.name: Sign in
A-02.intent: Get a returning student into the app in one tap where possible: biometric first on a known device, then Apple or Google, then email and password.
A-02.layers:
SignIn
├ StatusBar
├ Logo block
├ CredentialCard
│ ├ Email field
│ ├ Password field
│ ├ PrimaryButton
│ └ ForgotLink
├ Divider / OR
├ ProviderStack
│ ├ Apple (iOS only)
│ ├ Google (Android only)
│ └ Biometric (if enrolled)
└ CreateAccountLink
rules: Apple button shows on iOS, Google on Android; both on web.
Biometric appears only if a token is stored for this device.
5 failed attempts → 15 minute lockout and an email alert.
Staff accounts land on their role home, not the student home.

A-03.name: Create account
A-03.intent: Collect the minimum the studio actually needs, with WhatsApp as a first-class channel because that is where reminders and cancellations go.
A-03.layers:
SignUp
├ ProgressDots (1 of 2)
├ Heading + sub
├ FormStack
│ ├ First / Last row
│ ├ Email
│ ├ WhatsApp (+57 default)
│ ├ Password + strength
│ ├ Birthday (optional)
│ ├ EmergencyContact · name + phone
│ └ PhotoPicker · take or choose (optional)
├ ConsentRow → Terms, Privacy
└ PrimaryButton
rules: Email and WhatsApp must be unique; duplicates offer sign-in instead.
Emergency contact is collected here so it exists from the first booking, not only once a waiver is signed.
Password min 8 chars, strength meter, no composition rules.
Consent checkbox is required and stored with timestamp, IP and policy version.
Birthday optional — feeds the birthday WhatsApp/email automation.
Profile photo is optional and offered here, either from the camera or the library, so the front desk can recognise a student on arrival; it can be added later in Settings.
Colombia default country code +57.

A-05.name: Intention check — ¿Cómo quieres sentirte hoy?
A-05.intent: The signature moment of the product. One question, four verbs; the choice re-orders the home feed and the recommended classes for the session. The verbs are what the student wants to do, and each resolves to one of the four movement tags the rest of the system already colours by.
A-05.story: As a student opening the app I tap Respira and today's list leads with the slower classes.
A-05.layers:
IntentionCheck
├ Greeting (first name)
├ Question (display serif)
├ Subtitle (italic)
├ IntentionGrid 2×2
│ ├ Muévete → arde · hot, vinyasa, cardio
│ ├ Respira → fluye · restorative, yin, breathwork
│ ├ Equilíbrate → enraiza · strength, barre, core
│ └ Conecta → libera · community, workshops, events
└ SkipLink
rules: Shown once per day on first open; skippable.
Each verb maps to exactly one movement tag — Muévete→Arde, Respira→Fluye, Equilíbrate→Enraíza, Conecta→Libera — so the icon colour here matches the chip colour on every class card.
Selection tags the session and sorts Today's Classes by matching class_tags.
Stored as a time series — becomes a mood/practice insight later.
Copy stays in Spanish in both locales; it is brand voice, not UI text.

A-06.name: Terms & Conditions / Privacy Policy
A-06.intent: Real, linkable, versioned legal pages reachable from sign-up, settings and the website — with placeholder body copy until counsel supplies the text.
A-06.layers:
LegalDoc
├ BackLink
├ Title + updated date
├ SectionList (anchored)
└ CrossLink (Terms ⇄ Privacy)
rules: Each document is versioned; consents record which version was accepted.
Colombian data protection: Ley 1581 de 2012 and Decreto 1377 de 2013 sections are required.
Same content served to app and website from the CMS.
Anchors are stable so emails can deep-link to a clause.

S-04.name: Register & take payment
S-04.intent: The counter transaction in one screen: who they are, what they are buying, how they are paying. Built for someone standing at a desk with a person in front of them, so it is three short sections rather than a wizard.
S-04.story: As front desk I register a walk-in, take cash for a trial class and check her into the 7am without leaving the screen.
S-04.layers:
RegisterPay
├ Step1 · Who
│ ├ New / existing switch
│ ├ Name, WhatsApp, email
│ ├ Emergency contact, birthday
│ └ Consent checkbox
├ Step2 · What (reads plans.bienvenida)
├ Step3 · How they pay
│ ├ Cash · card · transfer · Nequi · PSE
│ └ Receipt by WhatsApp + email
└ SummaryRail
  ├ Order lines + IVA
  └ Complete and check in
rules: Products and prices are read from the value-model config, never typed at the desk.
Consent is recorded with timestamp, staff actor and policy version — the student agrees verbally, the desk records it.
Cash settles immediately; card and transfer create a pending order until the gateway confirms.
Completing the sale also checks the person into the class they bought, which is the whole point of doing it at the counter.
Every action writes to the activity log with the staff member's name.
states: Existing member: identity fields collapse to a found-member card
Payment declined: inline reason, order stays pending

C-08b.name: Cancel or reschedule sheet
C-08b.intent: One button on the booked class opens one sheet, because a student who cannot make a class is taking a single decision with two outcomes. Moving is offered first — it keeps the credit and keeps the habit.
C-08b.story: As a student who cannot make 7am I move to the 9:30 in two taps, and my credit follows me.
C-08b.layers:
ChangeSheet
├ Handle + title
├ PolicyLine (window from M-08)
├ BookingSummary
├ MoveAction (primary)
├ CancelAction (destructive outline)
├ ReplacementList (same day, same tag)
└ KeepBooking (dismiss)
rules: Move = cancel + rebook in one transaction, same entitlement, no fee outside the window.
Cancel returns the credit immediately when outside the window; inside it the credit is spent and the sheet says so before confirming.
The window value is read from Admin → Settings (M-08), never hardcoded here.
Replacements are same-day and matched on class_tags, then nearest time.
The front desk can perform either action on the student's behalf from S-02, which writes to the audit log with the staff actor.
states: Inside window: destructive confirm naming the forfeited credit

C-14.name: Preguntas frecuentes (1/2)
C-14.intent: Page 1 of the public answer sheet, split across two pages so the accordion never becomes a scroll of thirty open questions. It is the last stop before someone writes to the front desk, so it carries the same answers the concierge would give.
C-14.story: As someone who has never practised I read what to bring and how early to arrive without messaging anyone.
C-14.layers:
FAQ (2 pages)
├ Page 1 · C-14
│ ├ 01 Tu primera vez en HOY
│ ├ 02 Reservas y horarios
│ └ 03 Membresías y planes
└ Page 2 · C-15
  ├ 04 El espacio
  ├ 05 En camino
  └ 06 Contacto y concierge
rules: Questions are collapsed by default; only one opens at a time within a section.
Entries live in the CMS beside Club Rules, so the same answer serves app and website.
Anything about prices or plans links to #planes rather than repeating a figure.
Section 06 always ends with a route to a human — the FAQ never dead-ends.
states: No match in search: offers the concierge
Untranslated entry: falls back to Spanish

C-15.name: Preguntas frecuentes (2/2)
C-15.intent: Page 2 of the public answer sheet: the space, getting there, and contact — it ends with a route to a human, so the FAQ never dead-ends.
C-15.story: As a visitor on my way to the studio I find the address, parking and what to do if I am late, then message the concierge in one tap.
C-15.layers:
FAQ · page 2 (C-15)
├ PageHeader (2/2) + back to C-14
├ Section 04 El espacio
├ Section 05 En camino
├ Section 06 Contacto y concierge
└ ContactRow → WhatsApp / email
rules: Same accordion rules as C-14: collapsed by default, one open per section.
Address, hours and contact are read from studio settings (M-08), never typed here.
Section 06 always ends with a route to a human — WhatsApp first, email as fallback.
Anything about prices or plans links to #planes rather than repeating a figure.
states: Untranslated entry: falls back to Spanish
Studio closed today: hours row shows next opening

C-07.name: Bienvenida passes
C-07.intent: The way in for someone with no membership: four one-time options, stacked cheapest first, each one reservable on the spot. It is the other half of C-06 — whoever skips the plan lands here rather than at a dead end.
C-07.story: As a first-timer I take the trial class without signing up for anything, and I can see what a pack costs if I come back.
C-07.layers:
BienvenidaPasses
├ Header · title + sub
├ Eyebrow · BIENVENIDA
├ Intro line
├ PassList (vertical)
│ ├ Clase de Prueba
│ ├ Pase Individual
│ ├ Paquete de 3 Clases
│ └ Paquete de 10 Clases
└ FooterLink → C-06
rules: Prices read from the value-model config; no figure is written on this screen.
Trial class is one per person, verified by document or phone.
Packs expire per their own rule — one month for 3, three months for 10.
Every button enters the same single-screen checkout (C-04) with lazy registration.
C-06's skip link points here, so the membership decision is never a dead end.
states: Trial already used: that row drops to a note
Existing member: banner offers C-06 instead

P-01.name: Plans & prices — Modelo de Valor v3
P-01.intent: One value model, written once and read by every surface that quotes a price. Bienvenida lowers the barrier, Membresía is the primary plan with two ways to pay, Pausas and Regalos widen the offer, Espacio monetises the room outside class hours.
P-01.story: As someone deciding whether to join I see the whole ladder on one page and can tell what a month actually costs.
P-01.layers:
PlansPage #planes
├ Bienvenida — 4 cards + Reservar
├ Membresía (hero)
│ ├ Plan Mensual
│ ├ Plan Anual · Mejor valor
│ └ Footnote · ~$416.000/mes
├ Pausas y Regalos (two columns)
├ Espacio — 5 desde-prices + one WhatsApp CTA
└ TrustStrip · capacity + conscious controls
rules: Prices live in one config; no surface hard-codes a figure. Changing a price here changes it everywhere.
Membresía has exactly two options — Mensual and Anual. No third tier, no hidden discounts.
Espacio prices are 'desde' and lead to a conversation, not a checkout.
One class a day per person on any plan; the studio holds 15 mats and runs 4 classes a day.
Conscious controls: pause up to 30 days, leave without mazes, a kind cancellation window, notice before every charge.
Every plan CTA enters the same single-screen checkout (C-04) with lazy registration and local payment methods.
states: Member: Membresía cards show current plan and 'change'
Sold-out space date: CTA becomes an enquiry form

C-25.name: More · profile, rules, contact
C-25.intent: A fifth destination was one too many for a 340px bar, so profile, club rules and contacting the studio live one level down. Contact moves here from the floating bubble, where it competed with the primary action on every screen.
C-25.story: As a student I tap More and message the front desk, or read the hot-room rules, without hunting.
C-25.layers:
MoreSheet
├ IdentityCard → C-19
├ PrimaryGroup
│ ├ My Profile → C-19
│ ├ Club Rules → C-13
│ ├ WhatsApp the studio (outbound)
│ └ Email the studio (outbound)
├ SecondaryGroup
│ ├ Invite a guest → C-16
│ ├ Gift card → C-17
│ └ Settings → C-19
├ SignOut
└ BottomNav (More active)
rules: The dock carries four destinations: Home, Classes, History, More — every remaining screen is reachable from here in one tap.
Contact is outbound only — the rows open WhatsApp or the mail client. The app carries no inbox of its own; the studio answers where it already works.
The identity card doubles as the entry to profile, so the row above is not the only path.
Sign out is last, never adjacent to a destructive-looking row.
states: No membership: card shows the plan prompt
Outside hours: the WhatsApp row states the reply window

M-06.name: CRM · member 360
M-06.intent: One record per person that the whole studio trusts: who they are, what they have paid, what they have attended, and every conversation across WhatsApp, email and the front desk — with staff notes on the same timeline.
M-06.story: As a coordinator I open Mariana's record before she arrives and see she asked about a guest pass and mentioned a knee injury.
M-06.layers:
CRM
├ SegmentRail (all, at risk, new, no membership, birthdays)
├ MemberList (search, sort)
└ MemberDetail
  ├ IdentityHeader (photo, membership badge, consents)
  ├ MetricRow (LTV, visits, last visit, churn risk)
  ├ TabBar (Timeline / Bookings / Payments / Notes)
  ├ Timeline
  │ ├ WhatsApp message
  │ ├ Email event
  │ ├ Staff note
  │ └ System event (booking, payment, attendance)
  └ NoteComposer
rules: The timeline merges every channel in one chronological stream — WhatsApp, email, in-app thread, staff notes and system events.
Staff notes are internal and never visible to the member; health flags surface to teachers as a marker only.
Churn risk is derived from visit cadence against the member's own baseline, not a global average.
Front desk sees the timeline but cannot edit payments; Finance sees payments but not health notes.
Every view of a member record is itself written to the activity log.
states: No consent: channels shown as unavailable
Merged duplicate: banner with the merge history

M-07.name: All activity log
M-07.intent: An immutable record of everything anyone did, so a disputed refund, a deleted class or a changed price can always be traced to a person and a moment. Nothing on this page can be edited.
M-07.story: As the owner I filter to price changes last month and see exactly who changed what.
M-07.layers:
ActivityLog
├ FilterBar (date range, role, person, area, action type)
├ SortableTable
│ ├ When · Who · Action · Object · Source
│ └ Row → DetailDrawer (before / after values)
├ ExportButton (CSV)
└ RetentionNotice
rules: Append-only: no row can be edited or deleted by any role, including super admin.
Every entry records actor, role, action, object, before and after values, source (app, admin, front desk, automation) and timestamp.
Automations and system events are logged with the same shape as human actions.
Retained 24 months, then archived to cold storage; export produces a signed CSV.
Reading a member record is logged, so data access is auditable under Ley 1581.
states: Large range: paginated with a count
Export running: progress + email on completion

M-08.name: Studio settings & policies
M-08.intent: The operating parameters every other screen reads from: identity, hours, rooms, the cancellation and waitlist rules quoted across the app, tax and invoicing, and the third parties the studio depends on.
M-08.story: As super admin I change the cancellation window from 4h to 6h and every screen that quotes it updates.
M-08.layers:
Settings
├ SectionRail
├ StudioProfile (name, NIT, address, contact)
├ Locations → rooms + capacity
├ OpeningHours (per weekday, holidays)
├ Policies
│ ├ Cancellation window
│ ├ Waitlist claim window
│ ├ Late check-in grace
│ └ No-show fee
├ TaxAndInvoicing (IVA, DIAN resolution)
└ Integrations (gateway, WhatsApp API, email, calendar)
rules: Policy values are read at runtime by C-08, C-18 and E-02 — changing one here changes the copy everywhere, never a hardcoded string.
A policy change applies to future bookings only; bookings already made keep the terms they were made under.
Locations exist in the model even with one site, so a second sede needs no migration.
DIAN resolution number and range are required before electronic invoicing can be switched on.
Integration credentials are write-only in the UI and never displayed back.
states: Integration down: amber status with last check

E-01.name: Home · first-time empty state
E-01.intent: The home screen on day one, when there is no booking, no history and no statistics — it has to teach the next step instead of showing empty containers.
E-01.story: As a brand-new student my home screen tells me to pick a class and offers the tour, not a wall of zeros.
E-01.layers:
HomeEmpty
├ Greeting
├ EmptyState
│ ├ Illustration slot (placeholder)
│ ├ Headline + body
│ ├ PrimaryCTA · browse today
│ └ SecondaryCTA · studio tour
├ StatsPlaceholder (explanatory, not zeros)
└ BottomNav
rules: Statistics blocks never render as 0 — they render the sentence that explains when they appear.
The trial-class offer shows only if the student has not used it and Admin → Features → Free trial is on.
Announcements still render if active; they are studio news, not personal data.
Once a first booking exists this screen is replaced by C-01 permanently.

E-02.name: Payment declined
E-02.intent: A refusal is the highest-risk moment in the funnel: say what happened, confirm nothing was charged, keep the class reserved, and offer a way through.
E-02.story: As a student whose card was declined I switch to Nequi within the hold window and keep my 6pm class.
E-02.layers:
PaymentDeclined
├ ErrorBanner
│ ├ Title + body
│ └ GatewayReason
├ HoldCard · 9:00 countdown
├ AlternateMethods
│ ├ Other saved methods
│ └ Cash at front desk
└ ReleaseSpotLink (destructive)
rules: Never blame the card; state the gateway reason verbatim where one exists and keep it plain.
The spot is held 10 minutes from the first attempt; the countdown is visible and honest.
Three declines on one order switch the primary suggestion to PSE or cash.
No charge is ever captured on a decline; the order stays pending and the audit trail records every attempt.
Cash creates a pending order the front desk settles — the same path as C-05.
states: Hold expired: spot released, rebook offered

E-03.name: Class cancelled by the studio
E-03.intent: When the studio breaks the promise, the screen should do the recovery work: refund already done, replacement classes ready, no action required to get the credit back.
E-03.story: As a student whose 7am was cancelled I book the 9:30 instead in two taps, without contacting anyone.
E-03.layers:
StudioCancellation
├ CancelBanner (reason)
├ RefundConfirmation · 1 credit
├ AlternativesList
│ └ ClassRow ×2 (same day, same tag)
├ PrimaryCTA · book a replacement
└ ChannelNote (WhatsApp + email)
rules: The credit returns automatically before the student opens the app — the screen confirms, it does not ask.
Alternatives are same-day and matched on class_tags, then nearest time.
A studio cancellation never counts against a cancellation allowance.
Fires the class-cancelled WhatsApp template immediately, ignoring quiet hours.
If nothing suitable is available the screen offers the waitlist for the next occurrence.

E-04.name: Sign-in locked
E-04.intent: A lockout is a security measure that must not become a dead end: state the pause, count it down, and route to recovery, which is not rate-limited.
E-04.story: As a student locked out after five wrong passwords I recover by WhatsApp code instead of waiting.
E-04.layers:
SignInLocked
├ LockNotice
│ ├ Title + reason
│ └ Countdown 14:38
├ PrimaryCTA · recover password → C-19
├ SecondaryCTA · WhatsApp the studio (outbound)
└ SecurityNote
rules: Five failed attempts pause sign-in for 15 minutes and send the account holder an email alert.
Password recovery stays available during a lockout — it uses a different rate limit.
The countdown is server-authoritative; reinstalling the app does not reset it.
Never state whether the email exists; the copy is identical for unknown accounts.
Repeated lockouts within 24h escalate to a staff review flag.

C-20.name: Waitlist & claim window
C-20.intent: Turn a full class into a queue that actually converts: show the position, explain the rule, and make claiming a released spot a single tap inside a 30-minute window.
C-20.story: As a student I join the waitlist for a full 12:30 class, get a WhatsApp when someone cancels, and claim the spot from the notification.
C-20.layers:
Waitlist
├ StatusCard
│ ├ PositionRing (3 of 7)
│ └ RuleExplainer
├ ReleasedBanner (conditional)
│ ├ ClaimCountdown 30:00
│ └ ClaimButton
├ AutoClaimToggle
├ LeaveWaitlistRow
└ PolicyNote
rules: Promotion is strictly by position; the front desk can override with a logged reason.
A released spot is offered for 30 minutes, then passes to the next person.
Auto-claim consumes a credit the moment the spot is offered; without a credit the student is asked to pay.
Joining and leaving are free and never charge.
Studio-side promotion fires the waitlist WhatsApp template immediately, ignoring quiet hours.

C-21.name: Password recovery (WhatsApp OTP)
C-21.intent: Get a locked-out student back in through the channel they actually verified: a six-digit WhatsApp code, with email as the fallback.
C-21.story: As a student who forgot my password I receive a code on WhatsApp and set a new password in under a minute.
C-21.layers:
PasswordRecovery
├ Step1 · Identify
│ ├ WhatsApp / email field
│ └ SendCodeButton
├ Step2 · Verify
│ ├ OtpInput ×6
│ ├ ResendTimer 0:45
│ └ ChannelSwitch
├ Step3 · New password
│ ├ PasswordField + strength
│ └ SaveButton
└ BackToSignIn
rules: Code is 6 digits, valid 10 minutes, single use.
Three wrong codes invalidate it and force a resend; five resends in an hour lock recovery for 30 minutes.
Resend is blocked for 45 seconds and the timer survives a screen re-entry.
A successful reset signs out every other device and writes to the audit log.
Never reveal whether an account exists — the confirmation copy is identical either way.
states: Wrong code: cells shake, attempts left shown

toggles.label: Sign out other devices on reset

C-22.name: Manage membership
C-22.intent: Give members the three controls they actually need — freeze, change, cancel — without a phone call, while keeping the studio's notice periods intact.
C-22.story: As a member travelling for a month I freeze my membership instead of cancelling it.
C-22.layers:
ManageMembership
├ CurrentPlanCard
│ ├ Plan + price
│ ├ RenewalDate
│ └ UsageThisMonth
├ FreezeRow → date picker
├ ChangePlanRow → C-06
├ BillingHistoryRow → C-11
└ CancelRow (destructive) → reason sheet
rules: Freeze: up to 2 months per year, 15 days notice, billing pauses and the renewal date shifts by the frozen days.
Change plan applies on the next billing cycle; upgrades can start immediately with a prorated charge.
Cancellation keeps access until the end of the paid period — never a mid-period cut-off — and asks for a reason that feeds retention reporting.
A cancelled member keeps their credit balance and history; re-joining restores the profile.
Every change emails and WhatsApps a confirmation.

C-24.name: Notifications inbox
C-24.intent: One place for everything the studio has sent, so a missed push or a WhatsApp scrolled past is never a lost class.
C-24.story: As a student I missed the push about a released spot and find it in the inbox while it is still claimable.
C-24.layers:
Inbox
├ Header + MarkAllRead
├ TodayGroup
│ └ NotificationRow (icon, title, time, unread dot)
├ EarlierGroup
├ EmptyState
└ SettingsLink → C-19
rules: Every notification mirrors what went out on push, email or WhatsApp, with the same deep link.
Actionable items keep their action inline until they expire (claim a spot, rate a class, fix a payment).
Read state is per account, not per device.
Retained 90 days, then archived.
states: Expired action: row dims, action removed

C-23.name: Event detail & RSVP
C-23.intent: Sell the things that are not regular classes — sound baths, workshops, retreats — with their own pricing, capacity and guest rules.
C-23.story: As a member I reserve a spot at the full-moon sound bath at the member price and bring a friend.
C-23.layers:
EventDetail
├ HeroImage (placeholder)
├ WhenWhere
├ TitleBlock + hosts
├ Body
├ PriceRow (public / member)
├ CapacityMeter
├ StickyCTA · Reserve
├ BringAFriendRow → C-16
└ AddToCalendar
rules: Events price separately from classes and never consume class credits unless the coordinator allows it.
Member price applies automatically to active members.
Capacity is per event, independent of room capacity.
Cancellation window is per event and can differ from the class policy.
Deep-linkable for WhatsApp and Instagram.

C-01.name: Home dashboard
C-01.intent: The daily landing surface: what is happening today, what I have booked, what the studio wants me to know, and the nudges the studio needs (membership, feedback).
C-01.story: As a student I open the app and immediately see my next class, how long until it starts, and one thing worth doing right now.
C-01.layers:
Home
├ TopBar (logo, avatar, bell)
├ FeedbackPrompt (conditional)
├ MembershipNudge (if no plan)
├ AnnouncementCard (if active)
├ NextClassCard + countdown
├ QuickActions ×4
├ TodayList (intention-sorted)
├ StatsRow ×3
└ EventsStrip → BottomNav
rules: Blocks render in priority order; each is independently toggleable in Admin → Features.
Feedback prompt appears only for a class attended in the last 72h and not yet rated.
Membership nudge hides for active members and for staff.
Countdown shows under 24h, otherwise the weekday.
Today's list re-orders by the day's intention tags.
states: Loading: skeleton cards, no layout shift
Empty: no bookings → 'Reserve your first class'
Offline: last fetch with stale badge

C-02.name: Class schedule
C-02.intent: Find the right class fast. Two views (today, week) over one filterable list. Studio only — there are no online classes.
C-02.story: As a student I filter to 6pm intermediate classes this week and see which still have space.
C-02.layers:
Schedule
├ ViewSwitch (Today / Week)
├ DateStrip
├ FilterBar → FilterSheet
│ ├ Time of day
│ ├ Level
│ ├ Type
│ ├ Teacher
│ └ Room
├ ClassList → ClassRow
└ BottomNav
rules: Two views only: Today and Week. Month and recurring were removed — students book within the week, and a month grid answers a question nobody asked.
No 'Live Online' or 'On Demand' tabs — in-studio only.
A full class shows Waitlist; joining notifies on release with a 30-minute claim window.
Filters persist per device for the session.

C-02b.name: Class schedule · week
C-02b.intent: The week view of C-02: a six-column day grid of compact time chips, because comparing across days is the reason to open it. Same data, filters and booking state as Today.
C-02b.story: As a student I scan the whole week at a glance and spot the two evening classes that still have space.
C-02b.layers:
ScheduleWeek
├ ViewSwitch (Today / Week)
├ WeekHeader (Mon–Sat, selected day filled)
├ DayColumns ×6 → DayChip (time · open / full / booked)
├ Legend (movement colours)
└ BottomNav
rules: Tapping a chip opens C-03 for that class; booked chips are filled in the selection colour.
Past days are read-only; the current day is pre-selected.
Filters set on Today carry over to Week for the session.
Six columns, Monday to Saturday — the studio does not open on Sunday; a seventh column appears only if M-08 hours change.
states: Empty day: dash in the column

C-03.name: Class detail
C-03.intent: Everything needed to commit: what the class is, who teaches it, what to bring, how full it is, and how to reserve.
C-03.story: As a new student I read the class description and the teacher's bio before I book.
C-03.layers:
ClassDetail
├ HeroImage (placeholder)

D-01.name: Materials, tokens & physicality
D-01.intent: The material layer of the system: textures, surfaces, elevation and corner radii, with a switch between the styled build and the functional wireframe.
D-01.story: As a designer I fill a card with Warm Stone and set Medium Elevation, and every instance updates.
D-01.layers:
MaterialsPage
├ TexturePalette (sandstone, warm stone, clay, linen, travertine)
├ SurfaceScale (card, elevated, pressed, soft)
├ AccentSwatches (sage, terracotta, ochre, deep brown)
├ ShadowScale ×3
├ RadiusScale 8/16/24/32
├ TypeScale (Playfair / Jost / Quicksand)
└ ThemeMatrix (light / dark × styled / wireframe)
rules: Physicality comes from three layers, always together: an inset top highlight, a tight contact shadow, and a wide soft shadow.
Textures are fills, not images per component — one texture token per surface role.
Wireframe mode strips texture, colour and shadow but keeps layout and hierarchy.
Dark mode re-maps surfaces, never inverts the accents.
Minimum contrast 4.5:1 for body text on any material.

D-02.name: Component library — atomic
D-02.intent: Every component in the product, organised as atoms, molecules, organisms, templates and pages, so a developer can build a screen without inventing anything.
D-02.story: As a developer I need the class row: I find it under organisms with its states and props.
D-02.layers:
ComponentLibrary
├ Atoms (button, chip, input, toggle, badge, avatar, icon, divider)
├ Molecules (field+label, filter chip row, capacity meter, countdown, stat, price row)
├ Organisms (class row, class card, teacher card, roster row, plan card, nav bar, top bar, spec panel)
├ Templates (phone screen, desktop admin, legal doc, email)
└ Pages (the 30 screens in this canvas)
rules: RULE: the library is a living inventory. Any new element, variant or state introduced anywhere in the system is added here in the same turn, under its atomic tier, with its states — and retired components are removed and noted in the changelog. No component may exist in a screen without a library entry, and no entry may exist without a screen that uses it.
Atoms carry no business logic and no layout margin — spacing belongs to the parent.
Every component documents its states: default, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading, empty, error.
Touch targets never below 44px; focus rings visible in both themes.
Naming matches the code: PascalCase components, kebab-case tokens.
states: Default / hover / active / focus / disabled / loading / empty / error
